newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Acer unit says no impact from FDA flap.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Acer unit says no impact from FDA flap.

text.p: Taiwan computer monitor giant Acer Peripherals said on Monday a threatened U.S. import ban caused it briefly to halt shipments to the United States but the dispute had been resolved and no lasting impact was likely.

A spokeswoman said an Acer Peripherals plant in Taoyuan halted shipments for "two or three days" after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on October 19 told Acer it had found deficiencies in the firm's radiation testing procedures.
The issue was quickly resolved through consultations.
"The FDA gave us the clearing on October 26," spokeswoman Chen Tsai-wen said by telephone. "Shipments to the United States have already resumed and we don't expect any changes in sales."
Shares in Acer Peripherals, listed in Taiwan in July 1996, rebounded on news that the issue had been settled, gaining T$1.6 ($0.06), or 3.5 percent, to close at T$46.7 ($1.69).

"The news of FDA not issuing a ban is obviously good for Acer Peripherals and one that boosts investor confidence in the company," Foremost Investment broker Wang Jieh said shortly before trading closed.
The FDA's October 19 notice threatened to ban imports of Acer monitors if the testing deficiencies were not resolved in 15 days, prompting Acer to suspend shipments voluntarily.
The FDA dropped the threat after Acer Peripherals showed it had complied with U.S. quality-control requirements, the company said on Monday.
Company Vice President Joseph Hung said in a statement that the FDA issue would not influence the company's sales revenue in October or the fourth quarter of 1996.

Chen said that only the Taoyuan plant, which produces 50,000 monitors a month, was questioned by the FDA while its main plant in Malaysia, with monthly capacity of 200,000 monitors, had not come under scrutiny.

"Most of our exports to the U.S. come out of the Malaysian plant, while the Taoyuan plant exports only about 10,000 monitors to the U.S. per month. So the scale of influence is very small," Chen said.
Acer Peripherals has consistently said the discrepancy was over methods of testing and reporting, denying that its popular monitors were dangerous.
The FDA, which periodically inspects manufacturers exporting products to the United States, said it found deficiencies in Acer Peripherals' testing in a September 25 inspection.
Chen said Acer Peripherals would abide by FDA radiation testing guidelines in the future in order to avoid further shipment delays.
Acer Peripherals is a key member of Acer group and is the world's third largest colour monitor maker. It has factories in Taiwan, Malaysia and China.
In 1995, combined revenues at parent Acer group totalled US$5.8 billion.
